criteria.criterion: A test in secrets.rs shows scan_text on identical text twice returns findings equal to a fresh uncached scan, and different text never returns another text's findings (including secret-bearing then clean text). Run: cargo test -p athena-gate.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: the_text_memo_returns_what_a_fresh_scan_returns_and_never_another_texts passed, and all 119 tests passed. I read the test. It scans the token text twice and asserts both results equal scan_text_uncached, and asserts the fresh scan is non-empty. It then asserts the clean text scanned after the secret text returns nothing, and that the secret text still matches. It also checks that a Gitleaks with a different allow-list gets its own fresh result and does not share the first one's entry.

criteria.criterion: A test in checks.rs shows the new poll schedule still detects a fast completion, a slow completion, and a timeout of a long-running check with the correct status. Run: cargo test -p athena-core checks.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: the_poll_schedule_detects_fast_and_slow_completion_and_a_timeout passed. The existing a_check_past_its_deadline_is_killed and baseline_records_a_timeout_as_failed_with_a_note also passed; 21 of 21 passed. The test covers three cases: 'exit 0' (passed, exit code 0, no note), 'sleep 1' with a 30 s timeout (passed, exit code 0, no note), and 'sleep 30' with a 300 ms timeout (not passed, exit code None, note contains 'deadline', elapsed under 20 s).

criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new decision recording full cargo test --locked wall time before and after, labelled as measured on the job's machine with the method stated, and nextest (584 s vs 673 s, prior measurement) as a rejected alternative with the reason.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. New entry D126 (it follows D125) records about 651 s before and about 392 s after, labelled 'measured on this job's machine, 2026-10-25'. It states the method: cargo test --locked --quiet, summing each test binary's 'finished in' time, with a 'before' tree that had both changes switched off. It says plainly that this is not a wall-clock reading. It labels the earlier jobs' 444–466 s vs ~720 s as prior measurements. It rejects nextest with the reason that its 584 s vs 673 s (a prior measurement) is a smaller gain and adds a tool to the governed checks. The measured figure is summed per-binary time, not literal wall time (see the minor finding).

criteria.criterion: cargo test --locked passes in full, cargo clippy is clean and cargo fmt --check passes; no test is removed, ignored, weakened or filtered (git diff shows only added tests).
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks show cargo test --locked passed (1241 tests), clippy passed and fmt passed. The diff stat shows 1 deletion across the change, and the diff shows it is the non-test line 'std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));' in run_check. No test lines were removed or changed, and no #[ignore] was added.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for both changes. Only the four listed files change, and no governance files change.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat lists only CHANGELOG.md, checks.rs, secrets.rs and docs/decisions.md, and the working tree is clean. CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased 'Changed' entry that describes both the memo and the poll schedule and points to D126.

findings.summary: The recorded timings add up each test binary's time instead of measuring true wall-clock time.
findings.evidence: The entry says the times are 'finished in' figures summed per binary, leaving out build time and the gaps between binaries, and that it 'is not a wall clock reading'. The 'before' run used the candidate tree with the changes switched off, not the base commit, and each variant ran once. All of this is disclosed and labelled, so it is honest, but it is not the literal wall time the request names.

findings.summary: Every scan_text call reads config.toml from disk to build the memo key.
findings.evidence: memo_key calls std::fs::read_to_string(self.dir.path().join("config.toml")) on every call. This is cheap next to running gitleaks, but the text could be cached on the Gitleaks value.

summary: The change passes: all five criteria are met. It lands both speedups. First, a bounded per-process memo for `Gitleaks::scan_text`, keyed by the gitleaks binary, the generated configuration and the exact text. Second, a poll schedule in `run_check` that starts at 5 ms and doubles up to the old 200 ms without sleeping past the deadline. Each change has a new test, and I ran both. In `cargo test -p athena-gate`, the memo test passed with all 119 tests. In `cargo test -p athena-core checks`, the poll test passed alongside the existing deadline tests, 21 of 21. Athena's recorded full `cargo test --locked`, clippy and fmt runs all passed. The diff removes only the old sleep line, which is not a test. Only the four listed files change, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry for both changes. The new decision D126 records about 651 s before and about 392 s after, measured on the job's machine, with the method stated, and lists nextest as a rejected alternative using the labelled prior figures. One minor point: those times are each test binary's time added up, not true wall-clock time. D126 says so plainly. Whoever lands this may want a true wall-clock measurement later.
